The Strange Ox is a mysterious ox first encountered in the Emerald Grove in Act One.
“
Move along. I mean - moo.
„
— Zlorb, displaying its unparalleled ox impression

Involvement

Act One

Walking past the Strange Ox prompts a  DC 10 Insight Check to notice its odd behavior. A character who passes the check can talk to the Strange Ox via  Speak with Animals or a  Potion of Animal Speaking and make a  DC 10 Arcana Check to investigate further:

  • [ARCANA] The ox makes you uneasy. Try to discern why. (DC 10)
  • [ARCANA] There's something strange about this ox. What is it? (DC 10) (using Speak with Animals)

Passing this check confirms the creature is not what it appears to be.[1]

The party must successfully pass a  DC 10 Persuasion Check,  DC 10 Intimidation Check, or  DC 10 Deception Check to pressure the Ox into revealing its secret. On success, the Ox tells the party that it is heading to Baldur's Gate but refuses to elaborate further.

Attacking the Strange Ox in Act One causes its caretaker,  Toron, and neighboring oxen to become hostile. The ox drops pools of  Acid when damaged. On death, it drops a  Glyph of Warding: Acid that immediately explodes for 8d8⁠⁠acid damage.

If the party complete ⁠Raid the Emerald Grove and attack the refugees, the Strange Ox disappears with the other oxen when the grove prepares for the siege, and can be encountered later on.

Walking towards the Strange Ox in the stables of the Last Light Inn prompts a  DC 10 Insight Check to recall whether the player character has seen it before. Passing this check is not necessary to talk to the Strange Ox. With  Speak with Animals, the party can continue the conversation from the Emerald Grove. Regardless, the interacting party member must pass an ability check to continue:
  • [PERSUASION] Ah c'mon, now you've piqued my curiosity... (DC 14)
  • [PERCEPTION] You're the ox I met back in the grove. You were very hungry then; I saved you all, and now you have food. (DC 14) (if talked to previously with Speak with Animals)
  • [NATURE] You're a rare breed. An authentic Red-Backed River Ox. I thought you'd be more discerning... (DC 14)

On success, the Ox telepathically shows images of disfigured corpses with the sound of screaming in the background. Failing the check causes the conversation to end, but it is still possible to continue speaking with the Ox, essentially skipping the check.

Pressuring it to reveal its true identity results in the Ox threatening the party. The conversation can either end here or the interacting party member can continue asking questions. Questioning the Ox further causes it to revert to its native state: a cyan Phasm Ooze and enter combat with the party [3][4]. Before doing so, it tells the player character it was seeking a simple life of hay and a clean stable to live in. Alternatively, telling the creature its secrets are safe ends the conversation peacefully ( +1  +1  +1).

The  Dark Urge may relate to the ox's revelations and can tell it about their own murderous nature, to which it remarks they may be a kindred spirit, but it only wishes to be an ox. The player character can either respect or chastise it for not giving in to its bloodlust - the latter option causes the Dark Urge to brutally attack the creature mid-dialogue, killing it without initiating combat as it struggles to retain its ox form until the very end.[5]

Alternatively, The Dark Urge can, after sharing its violent visions, choose to respect its wishes by answering, "I don't care what you might be behind it all; you're an ox to me." The Strange Ox responds to the Urge's discretion by regurgitating a leveled gem as a gift.

If the protection surrounding Last Light Inn crumbles and the Shadow Curse falls upon the area, the Strange Ox disappears but manages to survive and can be encountered later on.

Act Three

If the Strange Ox survives into Act Three, it moves to Rivington at X: 36 Y: -149 on a hill west of the requisitioned barn. Approaching it triggers a  DC 10 Insight Check check to confirm its likeness. This time, the Ox is glad to see the party and has worried about the player character's health since the previous encounter.

As previously, the Ox can be questioned about its true nature and, as before, doing so causes it to deform into its natural shape and become hostile. Any other conversation path leads to initiating ⁠Help the Devilish Ox. If the player character decides to help, it turns into a  Strange Apple on the stable floor that can be picked up. The moment the player character enters the Lower City with it inside their inventory, the Ox declares, "Oh-ho! Thank you for the lift, my friend. Thank you very much indeed. Ta-ta!" The quest then ends and it disappears, leaving behind its  Shapeshifter's Boon Ring and a  Slightly Slimy Note.[6] If the party enters the Lower City before speaking to the Ox, it disappears and the quest cannot be started. If the quest was not previously started, the Ox cannot be recruited for ⁠Gather Your Allies.[7]

Completing ⁠Help the Devilish Ox allows the party to summon it using a  Gather Your Allies (class action) during ⁠Confront the Elder Brain. It reveals its true form as  Phasm, a type of Ooze with a true form similar to an Ochre Jelly which can shapeshift into different monsters with unique abilities during combat.[8]

Bugs

In Act 3, if the player enters the Lower City before meeting the Strange Ox in the barn and then goes back to Rivington, there is a high chance the Ox will not be present. The player character and party members will still make an intuition roll, but the Ox will physically not be there to be interacted with, therefore making its quest impossible to start. There is currently no solution to this other than to attempt to reload a previous save file or use third party programs to forcibly spawn the Ox.

Notes

  1. ↑ If the player character is a Barbarian, Druid, or possibly a Ranger, speaking with the Strange Ox may reveal it was discriminating in its choice of what kind of animal to present as: a rare Red-Backed River Ox.
  2. ↑ 2.0 2.1 In-game, it is incorrectly classified as an Ooze when it should be a Phasm
  3. ↑ The Strange Ox has a hidden passive that generates a 3 m (10 ft) radius  Acid surface when struck.
  4. ↑ If the Strange Ox is killed, the player character says afterwards, "I don't think I'll ever look at an ox quite the same." If killed in Act Two, Dammon then examines the remains of the dead creature and exclaims, "Just when I think I've seen it all... At least it's dead now."
  5. ↑ If the player character kills the Ox as The Dark Urge, no XP is gained. Additionally, doing so also causes Paladins to break their Oath.
  6. ↑ If the  Shapeshifter's Boon Ring was obtained earlier, the Ox leaves a random potion of moderate value in place of the ring.
  7. ↑ This can be fixed by using the third party Script Extender and typing the following: Osi.TeleportTo("49eb5b4b-c6ed-4d37-8f68-97b1128b7d56", GetHostCharacter()) This moves the Strange Ox to the party.
  8. ↑ The tooltip on the summoning action  An Apple a Day reveals the Phasm's name to be Zlorb while game dialog files refer to it simply as "Phasm".
